runners_data.name: Darkdeserthighway
runners_data.note: Ran on Good at Goodwood (10th/8f, recent) and has course-track sim-going experience; a natural hold-up horse who is likely to be closer to midfield than his ideal rear position given the field dynamics, so his closing effort may arrive too late over a bare mile.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Consistent recent activity (27d since last run) but his three runs on similar going show zero wins or places from 12 attempts; a prominent racer who will seek a position just off the pace but has a poor record converting that position into reward.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: Has one win and four places from 15 sim-going runs but that form has dried up recently (977000); holds a genuine late-running profile yet the traffic in this field means he will likely race in midfield rather than the rear he needs, blunting his finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Elman
runners_data.note: Has a fades-in-finish flag and his form string (740-00) alongside a step back to 8f from 12-16f trips looks a concern; the hold-up style and poor recent record on similar going make him a difficult proposition here.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good at Killarney (his most recent run, 12 days ago) which is directly relevant form; raced prominently and showed ability to travel to the front, with tongue-strap, making him one of the most in-form horses in the field on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Seti One
runners_data.note: Carries a fades-in-finish warning and has finished 13th, 13th, 12th in recent outings; the hold-up style and consistent poor recent form make it very hard to construct a winning case regardless of scenario.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 8f on Good going (including a Killarney win over 9f) and has a varied prominent style that puts him right in the heart of the likely race shape; 12 days fresh, headgear (hood), and a trainer running two horses from the same yard.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: Won over 12f on Good (most recent win) and has natural hold-up tendencies, but at 8f here is racing short of his best trip; redistributed into midfield rather than his preferred deep position, and the trip is a further concern alongside the style mismatch.

runners_data.name: Glamazon
runners_data.note: Placed four times from 14 runs on similar going and won over 10f on Good; Shane Foley partnership adds appeal and the prominent style fits this race shape neatly, though the step back to 8f from her last winning trip is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Hazrama
runners_data.note: OR=120 is clearly an error or misprint relative to the rest of this field; two runs, both well-beaten on Good going, and a fades-in-finish flag mean there is little evidence to support a competitive effort here despite the nominal rating.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Uncertain style (U) makes her tactically unpredictable; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a top-class booking but the form string (64-596) and zero wins or places from six on similar going gives little confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Magna Kotcha
runners_data.note: Fades-in-finish flag and only three career runs, all well-beaten; 87 days off the track is a significant freshness concern and there is insufficient form evidence to identify a winning scenario for this horse.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter with Colin Keane aboard for the in-form G M Lyons yard (5 winners in 14 days); STYLE_FIT note reflects this is mapped as prominent rather than a true natural front-runner, but the uncontested lead is still his to take and his recent form (2nd over 8f on Heav) shows he can finish.

races.paceDynamic: Cosmic Funk (Colin Keane, G M Lyons) is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner mile contest at Killarney and, with no genuine challenger disputing the lead, is set to bowl along at a controlled, self-imposed tempo — this is not a race where the pace will be forced or pressured from outside. Minaun View, Go Out, Land Of The Giants and Glamazon all carry prominent profiles and will jostle for early position behind Cosmic Funk, adding a degree of early bustle without fundamentally lifting the pace into genuinely searching territory. The field contains a significant cluster of true hold-up horses — Darkdeserthighway, Usuario Amigo, Timandi and Aurora Mist — who cannot all drop to their natural rear-of-field position given the distribution of running styles; those most likely to actually secure a rearward pitch are Darkdeserthighway and Timandi, with Usuario Amigo and Aurora Mist likely to be squeezed into midfield against their instincts. A controlled pace dictated by a single front-runner on Good turf over a mile is a race shape that classically favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, rather than those needing a strong gallop to close from deep — the prominent-to-midfield profile is the one to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cosmic Funk Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmic Funk dictates a comfortable tempo and the prominent group tracks efficiently into the straight.
scenarios.body: Cosmic Funk sets a measured pace and the horses positioned just behind — Minaun View, Land Of The Giants and Glamazon — get an uncontested tow into contention, with the winner emerging from this group as the hold-up horses lack the deep pace to reel them in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Late, Midfield Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is just quick enough that one of the midfield hold-up types, racing slightly out of role, times a run to snatch it close home.
scenarios.body: A strong final-furlong finish benefits horses like Aurora Mist or Timandi who are shuffled into midfield but retain enough natural finishing ability to pick up the pieces if those up with the pace tie up; the scenario relies on a stronger gallop than the lone leader is likely to set, making it a secondary outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Cosmic Funk is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and converts the solo lead into a sustained staying run that the field cannot reel in.
scenarios.body: Keane takes full advantage of the lack of pressure, setting a fractions that suit a horse at the top of its comfort zone, and the prominent horses behind either use themselves up closing or never get close enough; Cosmic Funk's STYLE_FIT flag is offset by the uniquely uncontested nature of the lead here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Off Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group engages in early scrimmaging for position and an unusually strong pace develops, burning out the lead horses.
scenarios.body: A fast-run race opens the door for a genuine closer to finish powerfully, but this scenario is markedly discounted because the true hold-up horses are redistributed out of their natural position and most lack the tactical speed to build a winning challenge from the rear in this field.

watchPoints.text: Minaun View won over this course and distance 12 days ago under similar conditions — watch whether Patrick McGettigan settles him in a tracking position rather than going forward, as his recent Killarney form makes him the most proven horse in the field on this exact race profile.

Cosmic Funk and the prominent group (Minaun View, Go Out, Land Of The Giants, Glamazon) may jostle for early position behind the lead, creating a busier-than-expected opening half-mile that could disadvantage horses with high draw numbers squeezed wide at the start.

Aurora Mist returns after 71 days off and is a natural hold-up horse being pushed into midfield — watch her early behaviour and whether Slattery can get her settled, as a fresh horse racing out of role could cause interference in the mid-pack.

Timandi and Darkdeserthighway are both genuine closers who will likely find themselves closer to the pace than they want — if either gets lit up early and races too freely, their closing kicks over a bare mile on Good ground will be diminished significantly.
Hazrama's OR=120 looks a data anomaly against an OR=63-70 field — verify market moves before race-off, as any significant support would suggest information the form book does not currently support.

runners_data.name: Cromac Quay
runners_data.note: Dropped back to a mile having won at 7f on soft and placed twice at a mile on good, this AP Harrington-trained filly has solid course-appropriate form and Shane Foley in the saddle; a natural prominent racer who should secure an ideal tracking position behind Green Carrera.

runners_data.name: Donna Time
runners_data.note: Rated 74 and stepping up markedly in class from handicap company, her best form has come over shorter at a mile on good but the step into Listed grade looks a significant ask; unclassified style adds uncertainty to where she will settle.

runners_data.name: Drop Dead Gorgeous
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's runner was visually impressive winning at Leopardstown on soft and her three placings on good ground give confidence in conditions; Wayne Lordan rides and she shapes as one of the key prominent threats if she can sit closer to the pace than her recent 10f starts suggest.

runners_data.name: Green Carrera
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, three wins at a mile on good ground and Dylan Browne McMonagle retain the ride; uncontested on the front end at a flat track and wearing a tongue-tie that has been present throughout her winning run, she holds the race by the throat early but the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder she is the structural pace-setter rather than a banked winner.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's filly has rattled off four wins in a row at 6-7f, all on good or soft, and steps up to a mile here; Chris Hayes rides and if she can transfer her front-foot speed to this slightly longer trip she could press Green Carrera for the lead, making her both a pace factor and a winning threat.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Attack
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll's mount is the most credible true hold-up horse in the field, with a win at 7f on good and placed form at a mile; 52 days off the track and stepping up slightly in class, but if the pace is strong he is the horse best positioned structurally to benefit from a fast gallop.

runners_data.name: Quiet Mutiny
runners_data.note: Pat Twomey's filly won over 6f on good and is on a retrieval mission after a 13th at a mile on good last time; a natural front-runner by inclination who will find herself pushed out of her preferred position by Green Carrera and Meriden — the STYLE_FIT discount applies and her recent mile form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Sinmara
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's second string was beaten into seventh at a mile on good last time and her only win came at a mile on soft; Declan McDonogh rides and she looks best suited to a scenario where the pace is truly strong enough to bring hold-up finishers into play.

runners_data.name: Sky Watch
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over and the horse carries headgear (p), but the form string reads oddly with hurdles distance entries in the history — the flat mile trip on good ground is the relevant form and a recent third at that looks workable even if class is a question mark.

runners_data.name: Spinning Around
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's runner won at 7f on good and on standard but finished eighth at a mile on good last time; a genuine prominent racer by nature who is squeezed into a midfield slot by the race shape — tongue-tie worn throughout and the STYLE_FIT note reminds that getting back to her best likely requires a prominent berth she may not find here.

runners_data.name: White Sand Beach
runners_data.note: LR of just 2 days is eye-catching and she carries a hood, with her best form showing multiple places at a mile on good; a hold-up type who has never won but placed consistently, she is well-suited structurally to a scenario where the front horses set a testing pace.

runners_data.name: Wild Bessie
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's filly won at 7f on heavy and returns after 72 days off; a natural prominent racer pushed into midfield by the pace compression in this field, the fades-in-finish tag is a material concern at a mile and the style mismatch makes her difficult to support at this level.

races.paceDynamic: Green Carrera is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no rival likely to genuinely challenge her for the lead, she should settle into a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front on this flat mile at Killarney. Drop Dead Gorgeous and Cromac Quay are the most credible prominent horses likely to sit immediately behind her, with Meriden also expected to travel close to the pace given her sharp, front-foot profile at 7f. This field contains more pace than the race shape can accommodate — Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, and Spinning Around are genuine prominent types who will struggle to find their natural positions and are most likely to be shuffled into midfield, with Green Carrera and Meriden best placed to secure the front two berths. A controlled lead for Green Carrera sets up a race where the prominent horses travelling smoothly just off the pace are the primary beneficiaries — horses like Cromac Quay and Drop Dead Gorgeous who can sit handy, conserve energy, and kick when the tempo lifts in the final two furlongs hold the structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Green Carrera dictates at a measured gallop and the race sets up for horses just off the pace to strike in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Green Carrera controls from the front while Cromac Quay and Drop Dead Gorgeous track in her slipstream, saving ground and energy before unleashing a sustained late kick; the uncontested early pace means stamina is preserved and a strong-finishing prominent horse is ideally placed to reel her in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds Rivals
scenarios.trigger: If Green Carrera's uncontested lead proves faster than expected and the chasing pack simply cannot close the gap in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Green Carrera, unchallenged and travelling kindly, sets fractions that are just brisk enough to blunt the late efforts of her rivals; her four wins from four good-ground starts at this trip underline that when allowed to dictate she is difficult to overhaul.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and string players closer to the front tie up, allowing genuine hold-up horses to come through late.
scenarios.body: Pivotal Attack, a true hold-up horse, would be the primary beneficiary if the pace creates a fast-run contest that brings closers into play; White Sand Beach has placed consistently at the mile trip on good ground and could benefit from a strong pace to sustain a run from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Prominent Logjam
scenarios.trigger: If the redistibuted prominent types — Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, Spinning Around — press forward and create a competitive early battle for position, inflating the pace.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected gallop would cause early burn-out among the pace-pressers and open the race up to a broader spread of finishing positions; this scenario benefits the horse with the highest raw ability who can sit midfield and produce a powerful sustained finish, but it relies on runners racing well outside their natural mapped positions and is therefore the least probable shape.

watchPoints.text: Green Carrera goes unchallenged to the front — watch whether Dylan Browne McMonagle allows her to roll along or deliberately softens the fractions, as the tempo she sets will dictate whether the prominent chasers or the hold-up horses have the winning profile.

Meriden's tendency to race prominently over shorter trips means she could press Green Carrera hard from the outset — if she does, the pace heats up and the scenario shifts materially toward hold-up finishers like Pivotal Attack.

Quiet Mutiny, Wild Bessie, and Spinning Around are all natural front-runners who are likely to find themselves shuffled into unfamiliar midfield positions — watch for any of them attempting to push forward early, as that would dramatically alter the race shape.

White Sand Beach's two-day turnaround and hood headgear are worth monitoring in the paddock — AP O'Brien running a horse back this quickly can occasionally signal a specific race target, and her consistent mile placings on good make her a structural interest in any scenario where the pace is truly strong.

Drop Dead Gorgeous steps back to a mile after two starts at 10f — watch how Wayne Lordan positions her early, as her one mile win came on soft and the question of whether she stays handy enough to use her sprint will define her chance.

runners_data.name: Arch Enemy
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with a recent win over 10f on good ground four days ago; Sam Coen (5lb claim) keeps the weight down and the horse's good-going form is solid, but style fit here is that of a genuine closer who may not get the test needed in a slow-run race.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and clear pace controller; Denis Hogan's yard is cold (1/19 in 14 days) and the horse is racing out of its most effective prominent role, but its ability to dictate unchallenged is the defining shape factor in this race — tongue-tie noted.

runners_data.name: Young Churchill
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes over on a hold-up type who placed over 12f on good ground most recently; trainer O'Brien has been quiet (0/3 T14) but the horse has placed five times in recent starts, suggesting consistency without the cutting edge to win from off the pace in a slowly-run affair.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing seven-year-old who won over 10f on heavy and has good-ground place form; blinkers fitted and Nicola Burns (5lb) claims here — one of the few horses with a natural tracking position, which makes this a live each-way profile if the pace is modest.

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Hogan's second string behind Tassarolo; a hold-up horse with a fade flag and a consistent record of double-figure finishes on good ground at this sort of trip, tongue-tie worn, making him difficult to recommend in any scenario.

runners_data.name: Kevin The Great
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll partners this four-year-old who has placed over 13f and 14f on good ground; tongue-tie fitted and zero wins from six starts on good ground is a concern, but the distance is right and any pace injection mid-race could play to his stamina.

runners_data.name: Limbocall
runners_data.note: Colin Keane, strongest jockey booking in the race, rides a horse whose natural home is at the back of the field — placed in the midfield band only because the rear is overcrowded; going form is limited (3 of 5 applicable runs on good), and the style-fit discount applies meaningfully here.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Fade flag attached to a true hold-up type carrying a 0.91 style-fit discount; one win from 12 good-ground starts and a record of fading late makes this hard to fancy even with the upside of a wider pace scenario, despite the distance appearing within compass.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's five-year-old has winning form on good ground at shorter trips and arrives six days fresh; blinkers fitted, Ben Coen is a live jockey, but as a genuine hold-up horse occupying an artificial midfield position, the style-fit drag (0.93) remains a real caveat.

runners_data.name: Voice Of Northeast
runners_data.note: A natural closer pushed into a midfield slot on the pace map; zero wins from 11 good-ground runs tells its own story, and a tongue-tie plus headgear combination suggests connections are searching for answers rather than holding a trump card.

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing six-year-old with a win on standard and multiple places; good-ground form is limited (0 from 4 runs) but the positional profile is one of the race's more tractable — hood worn and 27 days since last run is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes a rare spin on a horse whose 12 of 15 good-ground runs show no wins; a genuine hold-up type mapped to midfield through redistribution, carrying the 0.92 style-fit flag — the hood and jockey upgrade are the only positives.

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher
runners_data.note: Fade flag, zero wins from five good-ground starts, and a form line dominated by double-digit finishes; a true hold-up horse placed artificially in midfield, trainer A J Martin has one winner in 14 days but this runner's record offers little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Staying profile across 16-18f good-ground runs gives a tentative stamina edge, but fade flag, zero wins on good ground and a 0.91 style-fit discount combine to make this difficult to support despite the relative distance experience.

runners_data.name: Fantasy Fara
runners_data.note: Luke McAteer partners a hold-up mare with a fade flag and a form string dominated by single-figure finishes; hood worn previously, four days from last run matches several rivals — but 0 from 6 applicable good-ground runs offers no reason to upgrade.

races.paceDynamic: Tassarolo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, with no meaningful pace pressure identified, should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 1m3½f trip. Deuteronomy and Limestone Red are the only genuine prominent types capable of tracking closely, but neither carries the profile to seriously harass Tassarolo's lead, meaning the pace is likely to be modest and the race run in a compressed fashion with a late sprint premium. The field is packed with natural hold-up horses — Limbocall, Vervain, Alto Sax, Voice Of Northeast, Highway Sixty One, Monroe Dasher, Crypto Crash and Fantasy Fara are all true come-from-behind types but are mapped to midfield purely because there is no room at the rear of a race this controlled; their redistribution means the midfield is not genuine midfield, it is simply where they sit by default. This race shape — a lone front-runner, a slow-to-moderate pace, and a bunched field — strongly favours horses with a prominent tracking position who can quicken once the tempo lifts in the straight, rewarding Deuteronomy, Limestone Red and any hold-up horse bold enough to improve earlier than their profile suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tassarolo Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo dictates at a comfortable tempo and no prominent horse applies significant pressure at any stage.
scenarios.body: Tassarolo slides along in front, rations the pace through the middle sections and kicks clear entering the straight before the hold-up brigade can organise a challenge; the low-pressure lead insulates him from being overhauled by horses shuffled too far back. Deuteronomy and Limestone Red, sitting just behind, are best positioned to mount the nearest threat and should fill the places.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo's moderate pace allows Deuteronomy and Limestone Red to sit within a length or two and sprint past in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A compressed field with little gallop means the race turns into a sprint at the two-furlong pole, and horses who tracked the pace throughout hold a decisive positional advantage over those stuck in a slow-motion traffic jam behind. Deuteronomy's good-ground form at this sort of trip and Limestone Red's prior win experience on similar surfaces make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely collapses in the straight and a resurgent hold-up runner finds a gap late enough to run through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: The only way a genuine hold-up runner wins is if Tassarolo catastrophically misjudges and goes too fast early, stringing the field out and leaving horses like Alto Sax, Vervain or Arch Enemy able to pick off tiring rivals in the final stages; it is a low-probability scenario precisely because these horses are mapped out of their natural rear position and may not get the true test of stamina they need. Alto Sax's recent form line includes a win on good ground and Ben Coen has strong claims, but the redistribution caveat must temper confidence sharply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens Mid-Race Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a rival challenges Tassarolo sooner than expected, injecting an uncharacteristic surge in the middle portion and fracturing the field.
scenarios.body: Should Deuteronomy or Limestone Red push Tassarolo earlier than anticipated, the pace morphs into a true test and horses with strong stamina profiles — Kevin The Great, who has placed over this sort of trip before, and Young Churchill — could benefit from rivals who went too soon. This is the least likely shape given the modest pace credentials of the field, but a mechanical incident or jockey error could trigger it.

watchPoints.text: Tassarolo's early stride pattern — if Chris Hayes is forced quicker than ideal by Deuteronomy or Limestone Red pressing in the first half-mile, the race shape could fracture and change the entire tactical picture.

Deuteronomy's positioning under Nicola Burns (5lb claim) — as one of only two natural prominent types, how quickly she finds her slot in the first two furlongs will determine whether she can exploit the expected slow pace from a position of strength.

Colin Keane on Limbocall — the yard sent out a winner in 14 days and Keane's booking is conspicuous; watch whether he attempts to push forward earlier than Limbocall's natural style suggests, which would signal stable confidence overriding the tactical redistribution.

The going report is entirely unknown across all six available readings — any last-minute ground change from the anticipated Good could disproportionately affect horses in this field whose form profiles are surface-specific, particularly those with sole good-ground entries in their history.

Alto Sax's blinkers and Ben Coen's booking are the most eye-catching angles among the redistributed hold-up group — monitor market moves at the off to gauge whether Fahey's camp believes the horse can overcome its positional disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Loyal Touch
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up performer with a dismal recent sequence — six runs without a win or place in this form — and a string of mid-to-rear finishes at similar distances on good ground offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Party Dress
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare whose good-going record on the sim reads 2W4P over 15 runs, offering genuine placed potential, but headgear noted and recent form shows a long blank including heavy-ground defeats; unlikely to find the end-to-end pace here to suit a pure closer.

runners_data.name: Moyassr
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with one win on good going at a mile and a quarter, but this trip is significantly further than any of his best form; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a powerful booking yet the step to 1m6½f on a flat trip with limited pace looks a stretch.

runners_data.name: Coulstys Way
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a win and five places to his name over middle distances on good and yielding ground; 33 days off may leave him just short of peak sharpness, but he has the positional profile to sit in behind Lagoon Nebula and be competitive.

runners_data.name: Lagoon Nebula
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will lead on a flat track with no obvious pace challenger; has a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92, meaning the system notes she is technically racing slightly out of her sharpest profile, but that tag relates to positional mapping nuance — as the race's sole pace-setter she holds the key tactical role regardless.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a persistent fade-in-finish flag and a sequence of mid-to-rear finishes on good ground; the 8-day turnaround is short and the tendency to weaken late makes this trip at a moderate gallop look like an unfavourable profile.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Prominent/tracking type with strong recent form — two wins and three seconds over 13–16f on good ground — and W J Lee takes over in the saddle; the Paul Flynn yard is 4/26 in the past 14 days showing active form, and this horse's ability to sustain effort over this exact trip is arguably the most relevant profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Maarisha
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type placed in midfield on the map because the field is rear-heavy; her own best form came at shorter trips on soft or yielding ground, and 267 days off the track is a major red flag regardless of style fit.

runners_data.name: Sonic Invader
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse that the map places in midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; Colin Keane is an elite booking and the two recent thirds over 14–16f on good going show staying ability, but a STYLE_FIT of 0.90 and the reality of not securing his natural position tempers the chance meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Parish Express
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up runner mapped to midfield out of necessity — 65 days off track adds fitness uncertainty on top of a STYLE_FIT flag and a form string of zeros at this level; Bolger runners can bounce fresh but the evidence here is thin.

runners_data.name: Lauderdale King
runners_data.note: True closer placed forward of his natural berth on the map; the fade-in-finish flag is significant and his best form has come at shorter trips (10f) rather than this 1m6½f test, making his prospects at this distance and in this shape double-questionable.

runners_data.name: Folly Beach
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent type with no win or place at this track type on good going in recent starts; the 0W1P from 15 similar-going runs tells a clear story and the Jack Cleary claim does little to offset limited winning form.

runners_data.name: Celestially
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type repositioned in midfield; carries headgear (p), fades in finish according to the flag, and faces older handicappers at a demanding trip — the Donnacha O'Brien yard is active (4/16) but form figures of 10, 6, 4 show inconsistency, and the style displacement makes a bold showing harder.

races.paceDynamic: Lagoon Nebula is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 1m6½f handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — she can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop without being pressed into burning early energy. Coulstys Way and Baila Conmigo will look to track close up from prominent positions, giving Lagoon Nebula a small group to work with rather than complete isolation. The bulk of the field — Sonic Invader, Maarisha, Parish Express, Lauderdale King, and Celestially — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for all to find their natural rear-field position; in practice, the true hold-up horses may find themselves closer than ideal or stuck in traffic through the middle stages. On good ground over this extended trip with a lone, uncontested pace-setter setting an honest but measured tempo, prominent racers who can track the leader without burning reserves and then sustain their effort through the final two furlongs are most favoured — hold-up horses face the dual burden of an unexaggerated gallop that rarely produces the gaps closers need at Killarney's turning track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lagoon Nebula Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula secures the lead uncontested and sets a measured but honest pace that stretches the field from the front.
scenarios.body: Lagoon Nebula dictates from the front on her terms, with Coulstys Way and Baila Conmigo the nearest pursuers but unable to apply sustained pressure; on good going over this trip, front-to-prominent runners who conserve energy through the middle stages are rewarded as the race is run at a tempo too strong for closers to reel in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Lagoon Nebula's pace proves just sustainable enough for a close-tracking prominent horse to wear her down in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Jurality or Baila Conmigo, both with sound form at this trip on good ground, track within two or three lengths and produce a steady grind through the final two furlongs that the front-runner cannot repel; this suits horses that combine stamina with positional awareness rather than a late burst.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Mover Lands Spoils
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a horse repositioned from the hold-up group finds racing room to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Sonic Invader or Celestially, both genuine closers placed in midfield by necessity, benefit if Lagoon Nebula's tempo was deceptively strong and the prominent horses tie up inside the final furlong; this scenario requires a near-perfect run through and is materially discounted because these horses are not racing in their natural berth.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a contested early pace develops against expectations or the field concertinas dramatically on the final bend.
scenarios.body: A scrambled, uneven tempo would reshuffle the entire order and open the door for a fresh-legged hold-up horse finding daylight late; Moyassr's proven ability on good going at longer trips gives him residual claims here, though the scenario itself is unlikely given Lagoon Nebula's clear lead mandate.

watchPoints.text: Jurality (W J Lee) is the most dangerous attacker of Lagoon Nebula's lead — watch for him to be slotted in second or third position and whether he can sustain his effort through the final two furlongs as he has done in recent wins at this exact trip.
Lagoon Nebula's uncontested lead hinges on Coulstys Way and Baila Conmigo not crowding her early — watch the opening quarter-mile to see whether she gets a clean, pressure-free passage to the front.

Sonic Invader (Colin Keane) is a high-profile hold-up booking that will be displaced from his natural rear position — watch whether Keane elects to push him forward early or accepts an unfavourable closing berth, as either choice carries risk.
Maarisha returns from 267 days off — watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any sign of rustiness, as a long absence at this level in a competitive handicap is a significant unknown.

The going is officially unknown at Killarney for all six reports — watch for any late going description or market moves from yard-connected sources, as a ground change softer than good would materially alter the stamina picture for horses like Party Dress and Moyassr.
